description: This repository builds two images that have no upstream publisher -- obsidian-headless
is npm-only and Anthropic ships no Claude Code image -- and Renovate keeps both halves
of each image current: the base image on the FROM line, and the npm version baked in.
Merging one of these pull requests runs .github/workflows/images.yml, which derives the
published tag from the npm ARG and pushes it to ghcr.io.
The npm version baked into each image. Each is an `ARG <TOOL>_VERSION=` preceded by
a `# renovate:` comment naming the package, and the build workflow derives the
published image tag from that same ARG -- so merging one of these pull requests is
what produces the image. The FROM lines beside them are handled by Renovate's
built-in dockerfile manager and need no configuration here.
Majors here are real work rather than a pin bump: a Node major moves the runtime
under both tools, and a Claude Code major can change the flags a caller passes.
Label them so they are obvious in the pull request list and never merged on
autopilot.
Action updates are turned off because they cannot work here. The Renovate workflow
authenticates with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub refuses any push that
modifies a file under .github/workflows/ unless the token carries the `workflows`
permission -- which is not one of the permissions a GITHUB_TOKEN can be granted. So
these pull requests would fail to push rather than land, and the dependency
dashboard would list updates that can never be applied.
The actions in this repository are therefore bumped by hand. Enabling this again
means issuing a fine-grained personal access token with `workflows` write and
passing it to the Renovate action, which reintroduces exactly the long-lived
credential the GITHUB_TOKEN setup exists to avoid.
